TextBlock.Text: THEATRE The Biak enclave
DATE 14 November 2028 · 0410 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 90 min, closes at 135
E-7A Wedgetail — RAAF. Photo: U.S. Air Force photo by Lawrence Crespo · Public domain · cropped
"Air superiority is not guaranteed. It must be earned every day."
- Gen. Kenneth S. Wilsbach, Chief of Staff, US Air Force, 2025

BIAK, THE NEXT NIGHT. The Open Door's B-52s have gone back to the southern launch pool. LIGHTNING 41 to 44 are four RAAF F-35As carrying internal JSM from Langgur, supported by Grizzly's conventional SEAD pair, two Eagle IIs and Wedgetail 04. Suppress the new S-350 and S-300 engagement radars before committing the JSM package.

The mobile missile belt was delivered separately. The runway, Russian dispersal, Hind and Hip EW assets are present only if they survived The Open Door. Losing a complex removes its local fighter support, not the replacement SAMs. A standalone Second Ring starts with the surviving-defence case because it has no earlier damage record.

Destroy both engagement radars. The Buk, Nebo and Iskander are secondary targets; the relief ship and town remain protected. Prasetyo's ground crew have chalked a small red spider under the squadron board. Ward says it is not a kill marking.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.

FORWARD RECON: MOTH 11, a small RQ-7 reconnaissance UAV, joins over the local approach at minute ten, allowing time for initial air-defence suppression. The field team uses a portable launcher and local recovery lane. Two reserve UAVs are with the team from the start. They are unarmed and have finite fuel. Use their sensors to classify the military installations and update strike aimpoints. The small airframes are vulnerable; no scripted reveal grants a target solution. Keep a recovery margin and reposition the initial track as needed.
Wing Commander Daniel Ward; Captain Ratna Prasetyo at Langgur
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Use the four JSM Lightnings and the conventional SEAD pair to remove the two engagement radars. Check the current airfield damage report before planning the approach. Bring the package home to Langgur.
• Destroy the S-350's 50N6 radar and the S-300's 30N6E2
• Destroy the Buk-M3
• Destroy the Nebo-U radar
• Destroy the Iskander-M launcher
• Bring all four JSM F-35As home
• Harm no relief shipping
• Obtain a current classification of the land target area

Four RAAF F-35As with JSM, two RAAF Growlers, two F-15EX and Wedgetail. New S-350/S-300PMU2, Buk, Nebo and Iskander; surviving enclave airfield, dispersal, fighters and helicopters. Protected relief shipping. Forward RQ-7 field team: two reserve UAVs and a portable launcher; Moth 11 joins at minute ten.

The planned window is 90 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 45 minutes more; the operation is closed at 135 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
